Synopsis:
Outcome dialog between all important characters in the Steel Watch Foundry.Barchus may be dead so his participation is optionalToobin may also be dead, so his participation is also optional. If he is dead, he is replaced by a backup character representing the Gondians.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_Outcome.json: This scene takes place immediately after the player’s actions at the Steel Watch Foundry: the Neurocitor / lowest‑floor control centre that links the city’s Steel Watchers has been tampered with and Watchers are collapsing in the streets. Wulbren Bongle appears triumphant and vengeful, representing angry city survivors who view all Gondians as complicit, while Gondian workers (Menalda and possibly Toobin or a Gondian backup) plead that they were forced by the Banites/Iron Throne and beg for mercy. The player and a few surviving gnomes are on‑scene, catching their breath as Wulbren shifts from smug gratitude to a vow to eradicate every Gondian. Barchus and Toobin may be dead in some outcomes (or absent/replaced), and off‑screen factional tensions (Iron Throne remnants, Zhentarim middlemen, and Volo’s recent rescue) help explain why this confrontation is fraught and decisive.
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_Barcus_AfterOutcome.json: A completely optional dialog with Barcus after the outcome of the Steel Watch Foundry has concluded. After the other gnomes leave Barcus sticks around until the next long rest. He looks at the burning Foundry and will react to what decisions you have made.
- IRN_IronThrone_ReturnHostages.json: The hostage thanks the player for saving him and/or the other hostages. He will also beg the player to save their families working in the Steelwatch Foundry, giving them the quest if they don't already have it. If the majority of Iron Throne hostages AND the majority of Steelwatch Foundry hostages are saved, they will aid the player by making Steel Watchers on their side for the final battle. Otherwise they won't.Some variation based on whether the player has already been to the Steelwatch foundry and knows about the Iron Throne hostages, promised to help free the Iron Throne hostages, or doesn't know anything about them.If enough Iron Throne hostages survived, they should hint the player that they might reward them if they save their families. If not enough Iron Throne hostages survived, they should make it clear that the player will not receive any signifacant reward, other than narrative and thanks.If EscapedHostage has died, the dialog will trigger by talking to any one of the other surviving Gondians, but a Narrator will talk instead of all of them, as otherwise the permutations are too many. This will be an edge case, as EscapedHostage is very very likely to survive.
- END_GameFinale_TheHerosRevelry.json: Scene after DestructionOfTheBrain and before CombatOver showing the citiziens of Baldur's Gate reclaiming their city from the mind flayer threat.
- UND_GnomeForeman.json: The gnome leader's main dialogue. He thanks you for saving them, and tells you what brought his people to the Underdark to begin with - an expedition led by their charismatic leader Wulbren, to find a forgotten gnomish explosive of awesome power - runepowder.

context: The scene occurs immediately after the player sabotaged the Neurocitor at the Steel Watch Foundry: Watchers are collapsing in the streets and the Foundry is smoldering while the player and a few surviving gnomes catch their breath. Wulbren Bongle, speaking for angry city survivors, arrives triumphant and quickly turns vicious — blaming all Gondians as parasitic and vowing to see them wiped out. Gondian workers (Menalda and, if present, Toobin or a Gondian backup) plead that they were forced by the Banites/Iron Throne and beg for mercy; Barchus and Toobin may be dead or absent in some outcomes. Off‑screen tensions with Iron Throne remnants, Zhentarim middlemen, and recent rescues (e.g., Volo’s) underlie why this confrontation is decisive for the Gondians’ fate.
